messages:
elaine_marketing: Hey runtime team — asking for a small focused rerun for the webinar lead-demo. We need concurrency behavior and cold-start regressions documented for the exact payload below. Can you take this? :pray:

sam_runtime: Yep, we can do it. Quick Q: which deployment should we target (hosted vs dedicated)? Also want the exact target percentiles you care about.

elaine_marketing: Hosted is preferred (customers will demo against hosted), but if dedicated shows materially different behavior pls flag it. We care about p50/p95/p99 and 99.9 tail, plus error rates under 1k concurrent virtual users. Also show CPU/GPU utilization and autoscale events.

jordan_eng: Can you share the exact payload and a short script we can use to reproduce? If you have a tiny script wrapper for the presenter that hits a stable endpoint, even better.

elaine_marketing: Payload below (short). For the webinar we want a deterministic seed so results match slides. Also want a cold-start scenario: idle for 20m then burst to 1k users over 30s.

elaine_marketing: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-65b-quantized-v2",
  "prompt": "Summarize product updates for a CFO in 3 bullets.",
  "max_tokens": 120,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "seed": 42
}
```

sam_runtime: Got it. Two notes: 1) quantized variant has slightly different kernel paths; we'll run both quantized and float16 to compare. 2) Cold-start behavior depends on warmup cache TTL — is 20m the real scenario?

elaine_marketing: Yes 20m TTL is realistic for our demo environment. If that TTL isn't currently set in staging, please emulate by cycling instances.

tina_prodops: I can schedule a staging window tonight (22:00 UTC) to avoid impacting other tests. Marking it as "webinar-demo-rerun". Any special log retention needs?

elaine_marketing: Keep traces + logs for 48h. We might ask for flamegraphs for a quick follow-up. Also please record the exact git/hash of the serving runtime and any kernel/driver versions.

sam_runtime: Acknowledged. We'll collect: 1) p50/p95/p99/p999 latencies, 2) throughput curve, 3) error counts, 4) GPU util, mem, 5) autoscale logs + timeline, 6) trace samples for slow tail. We'll provide a small summary doc and raw artifacts (json/csv) plus a reproducible k6 script. ETA: within 18 hours of the run.

jordan_eng: For the presenter script, use this k6 snippet to reproduce the burst pattern (can attach in artifacts):

jordan_eng: ```bash
# k6 example
k6 run --vus 1000 --duration 60s --rps 200 \
  -e TARGET_URL=https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -e PAYLOAD='{"model":"redwood-65b-quantized-v2","prompt":"Summarize product updates for a CFO in 3 bullets.","max_tokens":120,"temperature":0.0,"seed":42}'
```

sam_runtime: We'll tweak ramp to 30s to match the "burst to 1k in 30s" requirement. Also we'll tag the run with metadata: marketing:webinar-2026, sample-id: wm-176543.

benchbot: Run scheduled by sam_runtime at 2026-03-24T22:00:00Z (staging). Artifacts will be uploaded to: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/webinar/wm-176543/ once complete.

elaine_marketing: Amazing — thank you. One last ask: please flag any failure modes that would break the demo (e.g., 5xx > 0.5% or p99 > 2s) and call them out in the summary slide.

sam_runtime: Will do. We'll post the summary + links here when done and attach the k6 script and raw csvs. If we see anything odd during the run we'll ping @elaine_marketing immediately. :thumbsup:
